blocks.text: The short answer is 50 metres — the main pool at Bondi Icebergs is a full Olympic-length lap pool, carved into the rocks at the southern end of Bondi Beach. So when people ask me how long it is, I can say it with confidence: it's the same length as the pool you'd swim in at the Olympics, just with a much better view and the occasional wave breaking over the edge.

Here's the bit that catches a lot of first-timers out: Icebergs isn't a single pool, it's two. The one everyone photographs — the long, north-facing lane pool that sits right on the ocean's edge — is the 50-metre Olympic pool. That's where the serious lap swimmers, the winter Icebergs members and the sunrise regulars do their thing. Alongside it sits a smaller, shallower children's pool, which is calmer, gentler and perfect for little ones or anyone who just wants a relaxed dip rather than a proper swim.

Both pools are filled with filtered seawater drawn straight from the ocean, which is exactly why the water feels so alive compared to a chlorinated indoor pool. On a big swell the sea washes right over the edge of the main pool, topping it up and giving swimmers an unmistakable salty tang. It's one of my favourite things about the place — you're swimming laps, but the ocean is very much in the room with you.

For the classic photo of the pool set against the ocean, don't get in the water — walk the coastal path just south towards Mackenzies Bay, or grab a window seat upstairs at the club. You get that iconic elevated angle looking straight down the 50-metre lanes to the sea.
Why an Olympic-length pool matters here

The 50-metre length isn't a coincidence. Bondi Icebergs has been a home for winter ocean swimming since 1929, and the pool was rebuilt and expanded to full Olympic dimensions in the 1930s. That heritage is why it still draws lap swimmers, triathletes in training and the famous Icebergs winter swimming club, who take the plunge through the coldest months of the year. If you want to actually clock your distance, one length is 50 metres and a there-and-back lap is 100 metres — handy maths if you're setting yourself a target.

blocks.title: It's a working club pool, not a resort
blocks.text: Icebergs is a genuine swimming club and public pool, so it sometimes closes for maintenance (typically a weekday each week) and for the occasional event or competition. Entry fees, opening hours and closures do change, so I'd always check the official Icebergs website or give them a call before you make a special trip.

You don't need to be a member or a champion to swim here — the pool is open to the public for a small entry fee, and that fee covers both the main pool and the children's pool. Bring goggles if you actually want to swim laps, because the ocean water isn't crystal-clear and the sun glare off the surface is strong. There's a sauna, changing rooms and, up above, the well-known Icebergs dining room and bar if you'd rather admire those 50 metres with a drink in hand than swim them.

items.q: How long is the Bondi Icebergs pool?
items.a: The main pool is 50 metres long — a full Olympic-length lap pool. There's also a separate, smaller children's pool beside it for shallower, more relaxed swimming.

items.q: Is the Bondi Icebergs pool Olympic size?
items.a: Yes. The main lap pool is 50 metres, the standard Olympic length, which is why it's popular with serious swimmers and the club's winter swimming members.

items.q: Are there two pools at Bondi Icebergs?
items.a: Yes — a 50-metre main lap pool right on the ocean edge, and a smaller, shallower children's pool alongside it that's better suited to families and casual swimmers.

items.q: Is the pool saltwater or chlorinated?
items.a: Both pools are filled with filtered seawater drawn from the ocean. On a big swell, waves wash straight over the edge of the main pool and top it up.

items.q: Can anyone swim at Bondi Icebergs?
items.a: Yes, it's open to the public for a small entry fee — you don't need to be a member. Hours, fees and maintenance closures change, so check the official Icebergs website before you go.

blocks.text: So next time someone asks you how long the Icebergs pool is, you'll know: 50 metres of Olympic-length, wave-topped seawater, hanging off the rocks at the end of one of the most famous beaches in the world. There aren't many better places to knock out a few laps.
